{"thought": "The crash is in `TMS320C64x_insn_name` which is a global-buffer-overflow READ 8. The fuzzer target is `fuzz_disasmnext` which uses the "next" branch of capstone. 

Looking at the fuzz harness, the first byte of input selects the platform (architecture). Item 27 is `CS_ARCH_TMS320C64X` with `CS_MODE_BIG_ENDIAN`. The platforms array has 28 items (0-27) in the master version, and 29 (0-28) in the next version (which has WASM as item 28).

For the "next" version, `platforms_len` would be 29. To select item 27 (TMS320C64X), we need `Data[0] % 29 == 27`. So Data[0] could be 27.

The crash is in `TMS320C64x_insn_name` - a global buffer overflow when reading an instruction name. This likely means that when disassembling TMS320C64X instructions, some instruction ID exceeds the bounds of the name lookup table.

Let me look at the TMS320C64X code to understand the vulnerability better."}
